people.name: Amanda Kahlow

people.name: Piyush Chitkara
people.bio: Co-founder of Accacia, involved in building out the company's platform and product.

people.name: László Kishonti
people.bio: Hungarian technology entrepreneur who founded Kishonti Ltd., a graphics and compute benchmarking/engineering company, and spun AIMotive out of it in 2015 to build AI-based autonomous driving software and accelerator IP. He has led the company as CEO through its development of the aiDrive and aiWare platforms.

people.name: Jeff Cardenas
people.bio: Co-founder and CEO of Apptronik; previously co-founded and led startups in Austin before focusing on commercializing humanoid robots.

people.name: Luis Sentis
people.bio: Co-founder and robotics professor at the University of Texas at Austin, where he directed the Human Centered Robotics Lab that incubated the technology behind Apptronik.

people.name: Nicholas Paine
people.bio: Co-founder and CTO; robotics engineer with a background in humanoid controls and legged locomotion, formerly with the University of Texas Human Centered Robotics Lab.

people.name: Aaron Brown
people.bio: Co-Founder of Archimetis; former leader of Google's developer infrastructure initiatives.

people.name: Paul Manwell
people.bio: Co-Founder and CEO of Archimetis; former Chief of Staff to Google CEO Sundar Pichai.

people.name: Emanuele Ostuni
people.bio: Leader of ARTBIO since its launch, guiding the company's strategy to build a differentiated pipeline of Pb-212 based alpha radioligand therapies and an integrated isotope supply chain.

people.name: Carina Hong
people.bio: Carina Letong Hong is the founder and CEO of Axiom Math. Born in Guangzhou, China, she earned a bachelor's degree in mathematics and physics from MIT, where she wrote nine research papers and took 20 advanced mathematics courses, and was a Morgan Prize winner. A Rhodes Scholar at the University of Oxford, she later pursued a joint law degree and PhD at Stanford before dropping out to start Axiom Math. She has described her thesis bluntly as "Math is AGI," arguing that combining computation with mathematical proofs yields real-time verification of code that works.

people.name: Shubho Sengupta
people.bio: Former Meta AI researcher who worked on large language models that wrote software tests; the first member and now CTO of Axiom Math.

people.name: Ru Liyun (茹立云)
people.bio: Former Sogou COO and long-time deputy to Wang Xiaochuan; joined Baichuan's founding team to lead product and operations.

people.name: Wang Xiaochuan (王小川)
people.bio: Former CEO of Chinese search company Sogou (sold to Tencent in 2021) and a Tsinghua University-trained computer scientist. Founded Baichuan in April 2023 to build large language models and AI healthcare products; has publicly framed Baichuan's mission as 'superintelligence in the service of health and happiness.'

people.name: Neelakantha Bhanu Prakash
people.bio: Widely known as the 'world's fastest human calculator' and a global mental-math champion; founded Bhanzu to help students overcome math fear and build calculation speed through live online math classes.

people.name: Daniel Jung
people.bio: Co-founder of Branch International, involved in the company's early product and technology build-out for mobile lending in emerging markets.

people.name: Matt Flannery
people.bio: Co-founder of Kiva and co-founder/CEO of Branch International; focused on expanding access to credit and financial services for underserved consumers in emerging markets.

people.name: Alan Budiarto
people.bio: Co-founder of BRIK, which focuses on B2B cloud manufacturing to simplify Indonesia's construction supply chain.

people.name: Francis Anugerah
people.bio: Founded BRIK in 2022; previously founder of IDExpress. BRIK has grown to more than US$25 million in total funding from global investors.

people.name: Francis Anugrah
people.bio: Founder of BRIK — previously worked in Finance and Investments across Beijing, Singapore, London, Jakarta and Mumbai. A secondment into a portfolio company, Siam City Cement in Thailand, gave him first-hand insight into the construction industry and its lack of innovation. He also co-founded IDExpress. BRIK was born in May 2022 as a direct-to-user construction materials aggregator developing affordable, next-generation products for Indonesia's construction sector.

people.name: Ria Astika
people.bio: Co-founder of BRIK, the Indonesia-based B2B building materials and construction solutions startup established in 2022.

people.name: Willuam Lunt
people.bio: Co-founder of BRIK, established in 2022 to address price transparency, material quality and inefficient logistics in construction.

people.name: Alok Chanani
people.bio: Former United States Army Captain and serial entrepreneur. Co-founded BuildOps in 2018 with Steve Chew in Los Angeles after seeing contractors running multimillion-dollar operations on spreadsheets and WhatsApp. Named to the Los Angeles Business Journal's 2026 LA500 list of the 500 most influential executives in Los Angeles. Has stated: "The men and women in the trades are the people who keep this country running, and they deserve technology built with the same sophistication they bring to their own work."

people.name: Steve Chew
people.bio: Co-founded BuildOps alongside Alok Chanani. Previously helped lead cloud strategy for Outlook & Exchange at Microsoft; has spoken about witnessing the construction and commercial contractor industry transform through emerging technologies.

people.name: Chris Altchek
people.bio: Founder and CEO of Cadence, which he founded in 2020 after previously co-founding internet media company Mic; earlier background in investment banking. Runs Cadence as a privately held company focused on bringing hospital-level chronic care into patients' homes.

people.name: Kareem Zaki
people.bio: Co-founder of Cadence and a General Partner at Thrive Capital; also a co-founder of Cedar.

people.name: Elaine Sullivan
people.role: Founder; Executive Entrepreneur and Advisor to the Board of Directors
people.bio: Founder of Carrick and CEO since 2016. The company noted she took Carrick from inception to a company with multiple clinical assets in a short period of time; she transitioned leadership to Tim Pearson in 2019 and continues to drive the company forward as Executive Entrepreneur and Advisor to the Board of Directors.

people.name: Aaron Tan
people.bio: Co-founder and Group CEO of Carro. He leads the group's differentiated ecosystem-led business model, focused on marketplace margin expansion, cross-selling ancillaries to drive recurring income and customer lifetime value, and expansion into new markets and segments, particularly NEVs. Under his leadership Carro launched its Brand New segment in Singapore and Malaysia to capture a broader customer base across the automotive value chain and reported record FY2025 revenues of S$1.2 billion.

people.name: Ashok Subramanian
people.bio: Ashok Subramanian co-founded Centivo in 2017 and serves as Chief Executive Officer. He has worked in the self-funded health plan space for 20 years, including nine years as co-founder and CEO of Liazon, a private benefits exchange for active employees that was acquired by Towers Watson in 2013. He founded Centivo because he felt it was time to radically transform the American healthcare system, noting that over half of Americans can't afford a $400 expense yet the average American family deductible is over $3,800.

people.name: Andrew McLeod
people.bio: Founded Certn in 2016 and runs it as CEO. Described the company's mission as leading in human risk intelligence solutions so organizations and individuals can connect and gain trust in one another, and stated that funding would be used to grow Certn's products beyond North America and facilitate trusted connection on a global scale.

people.name: Wen H. Hsieh
people.role: Board of Directors (founding managing partner, Matter Venture Partners)

people.name: William Yang Wang
people.bio: Founder and CEO of ChipAgents. Founded the company in 2024. A UC Santa Barbara professor who previously worked on Amazon Q at AWS. He describes ChipAgents as building toward chip superintelligence, bringing together the ontology, full-flow, language-model, and physical-model layers needed for fully autonomous, self-improving AI across the semiconductor design flow.

people.name: Andy Yin
people.bio: Co-founder and CEO of Cloudwise, based in Chaoyang District, Beijing, China. Focuses on SaaS software development and technologies, and cloud computing. Studied at Tsinghua University. Company website listed on his profile.

people.name: Bin Tan
people.bio: Co-founder of Cloudwise, founded the company in 2009 alongside Andy Yin.

people.name: Alex Showalter-Bucher
people.bio: Co-founder and SVP of Technology at Code Metal. An AI researcher who previously worked at MIT Lincoln Laboratory and is listed as a founder of the company in 2023.

people.name: Peter Morales
people.bio: Co-founder and CEO of Code Metal. Previously technology chief at a gaming company and worked at BAE Systems, MIT Lincoln Laboratory and Microsoft. He started thinking about the challenge of writing code for hardware systems while at BAE Systems roughly a decade ago, helping write software for the F-35 fighter to counteract enemy radar and porting machine-learning algorithms into the aircraft's chips. He co-founded Code Metal with Alex Showalter-Bucher to solve the problem of making software work for particular hardware environments.

people.name: Neeraj Khandelwal
people.bio: Co-founder of CoinDCX, the Mumbai-based crypto exchange founded in April 2018 that became India's first unicorn crypto startup.

people.name: Sumit Gupta
people.bio: Co-founder of CoinDCX, India's cryptocurrency exchange. Referenced as representing CoinDCX in commentary on cryptocurrency market declines and long-term investor opportunities.

people.name: Nazneen Rajani
people.bio: After leaving her position as research lead at the AI startup Hugging Face, Rajani founded Collinear AI to focus on helping businesses control and customize AI models. 'There was no clear evaluation for checking whether a model was ready to launch, or the type of things people should be thinking about before putting their models into production,' she says. 'I wanted to make a dent in it.' Her team works on updating pre-trained LLMs with client-specific information and on making a model safe without sacrificing performance, using a process called auto-alignment where an AI judge curates good and bad training examples.

people.name: Soumyadeep Bakshi
people.bio: Soumyadeep's work spans data strategy, verification, and evaluation infrastructure. Before Collinear AI, he led Deloitte's AI practice, advising frontier labs on data for model development.

people.name: Luke Hansen
people.bio: Born into the contractor life as a member of the Hansen family roofing business. While roofing houses, taking and organizing photos became central to their process; unable to find a solution, the Hansens decided to build their own app. CompanyCam was tested and adjusted on their real roofing projects before launching, and now serves 140k+ contractors with over 1 billion photos taken in the app.

people.name: Michael Marmo
people.bio: Fourth-generation waste industry professional. Started as a scale operator at a local transfer station, then founded Curbside, a New York City hauling company focused on C&D waste, where he invested early in a digital operations platform. After selling Curbside to Cogent Waste Services, he launched CurbWaste to help haulers digitize nationally. He describes CurbWaste as 'a software for haulers, by haulers' and 'the modern operating system for waste haulers.'

people.name: Chandrashekhar Sohoni
people.bio: Ex-Nokia employee who co-founded Newshunt (later DailyHunt) in 2009.

people.name: Umang Bedi
people.bio: Former Facebook India managing director; co-founder of VerSe Innovation, parent of DailyHunt and Josh.

people.name: Umesh Kulkarni
people.bio: Ex-Nokia employee who co-founded Newshunt (later DailyHunt) in 2009.

people.name: Virendra Gupta
people.bio: Acquired Newshunt in 2011 and renamed it DailyHunt in 2015; founder of VerSe Innovation, the parent company of DailyHunt and Josh.

people.name: Aaron LaRue
people.bio: Co-founder of Deferred; part of a founding team that previously worked together across multiple startups and successful exits, including Open Listings and Balance Homes.

people.name: Alexander Farrill
people.bio: Co-founder of Deferred; part of the founding trio alongside Judd Schoenholtz and Aaron LaRue, building a technology-driven platform to make 1031 exchanges accessible to all investors.

people.name: Judd Schoenholtz
people.bio: Co-founder of Deferred; previously co-founded Open Listings (acquired by Opendoor) and Balance Homes (acquired by EasyKnock). Leads Deferred's effort to scale the most modern, secure, and transparent 1031 exchange platform with a No Fee model.

people.name: Dave Ferguson
people.bio: Co-founder of EeroQ (founded 2016), listed among the company's founders in company profiles.

people.name: Faye Wattleton
people.bio: Co-founder of EeroQ (founded 2016), listed among the company's founders in company profiles.

people.name: Nick Farina
people.bio: Co-founder and CEO of EeroQ since co-founding the company in 2017. Named to Crain's Chicago Business 40 Under 40 for leading EeroQ's differentiated quantum computing approach using single electrons on superfluid helium, and for growing the company from a self-funded startup into one backed by B Capital, the State of Illinois INVENT Fund and other leading investors.

people.name: Hung Pham
people.bio: Co-founder of Eureka Robotics, which was founded by Pham Quang Cuong and Hung Pham in 2018 as a spin-off from Nanyang Technological University (NTU).

people.name: Pham Quang Cuong
people.bio: Associate Professor at NTU Singapore who came to Singapore in 2013 and led the research group behind the IKEA chair-assembling robot (published in Science Robotics). He founded Eureka Robotics in 2018 as an NTU spin-off and serves as CEO, overseeing key corporate decisions, operations, and resources. He has stated the mission is 'to automate the dull, dirty, and dangerous, allowing humans to focus on creativity.'

people.name: Rami Karabibar
people.bio: Co-founder and CEO of EvenUp. Karabibar has emphasized the company's mission to close the justice gap and its vision for deep transparency in the personal injury industry, stating that legal AI is becoming the backbone of personal injury law.

people.name: Raymond Mieszaniec
people.bio: Co-founder and COO of EvenUp. A childhood experience with a family car accident that left his father permanently disabled shaped his mission to level the playing field in the legal system. He leads operations focused on helping law firms maximize claim value.

people.name: Saam Mashhad
people.bio: Co-founder and Chief Product Officer of EvenUp and a former litigation attorney. He helps shape the product vision combining AI, legal expertise, and structured case data.

people.name: Alessio Signorini
people.bio: Co-Founder and Chief Technology Officer of Evidation; shared Evidation's founding story on the AWS Health Innovation Podcast.

people.name: Luca Foschini
people.bio: Co-founder of Evidation, founded in 2012 as a real-world health data insights company providing better healthcare decisions and research.

people.name: Eugene A. Bauer, MD
people.bio: Co-founded Evommune and serves as Chief Medical Officer; former senior leader at Dermira, Inc.

people.name: Hans Hofland, PhD
people.bio: Co-founded Evommune and leads research; former senior leader at Dermira, Inc.

people.name: Luis Peña
people.bio: Luis Peña founded Evommune in 2020 and serves as President and CEO. He previously co-founded Dermira and held leadership roles at Stiefel (SVP Portfolio Planning and Management), Connetics, Theravance and Genentech. He emphasizes organizational culture, emotional intelligence and investment in training as core leadership principles.

people.name: Guillaume Bouvard
people.bio: Listed among employees at Extend. Extend was founded in 2017 by industry veterans of American Express, Capital One, and other Fortune 500 companies.

people.name: Prabhakar Reddy
people.bio: Co-founded FalconX in 2018. FalconX is an online platform offering cryptocurrency trading and investment solutions for institutions, now valued at $8B.

people.name: Raghu Yarlagadda
people.bio: CEO and Co-Founder of FalconX. On the bloXroute acquisition he said: "We believe the future of capital markets will be onchain. As onchain and traditional markets continue to converge, institutions will need a single platform built for both. bloXroute strengthens our platform and accelerates our ability to build the products and services institutions will rely on as markets evolve."

people.name: Jack Norbeck
people.bio: Jack Norbeck is Co-Founder and Chief Technology Officer of Fervo Energy. He met co-founder Tim Latimer while the two were earning degrees at Stanford University.

people.name: Tim Latimer
people.bio: CEO and Co-Founder of Fervo Energy. He has publicly highlighted the company's transition from technology breakthroughs to large-scale deployment, particularly at Cape Station, and has spoken about growing policy awareness in Washington of geothermal's importance as a firm, land-efficient clean power source.

people.name: Lorien Gabel
people.bio: Co-founder of Figment and its CEO; referenced in coverage as the leader whose 'Big Bet on Staking Has Paid Off.' An investor noted he has been backing founders Lorien and Matt for the past 20 years, citing the founding team's decades of experience building and scaling internet infrastructure companies.

people.name: Matt Harrop
people.bio: Listed among Figment's employees and referenced as one of the founding team ('founders Lorien and Matt') whose prior experience successfully building and scaling multiple internet infrastructure companies paved the foundation for Figment's position as a top infrastructure and tool provider.

people.name: Chris Maddern
people.bio: Co-founder of e-commerce firm Button and former head of mobile at Venmo. Leads Floor, which he describes as making users 'a smarter, more connected human with the tokens that you're purchasing.'

people.name: Christine Brown
people.bio: Robinhood Crypto's first COO and the face of its crypto business until she left at the end of March 2022, when she said she was 'starting a crypto venture.' She joined Floor as COO, touting the app as a solution to the 'nightmare scenario' of tracking NFT price movement over time on marketplaces like OpenSea.

people.name: Siddhartha Dabral
people.bio: Also listed as Sid Dabral; co-founder of e-commerce firm Button and co-founder/CTO of Floor, overseeing the technology behind its cross-chain NFT portfolio tracking platform.

people.name: John Haskell
people.bio: Co-founder of Flourish Health alongside Natalia Birgisson and Josh Gachnang; has built and scaled payer-facing behavioral health businesses before.

people.name: Josh Gachnang
people.bio: Co-founder of Flourish Health alongside Natalia Birgisson and John Haskell; has built and scaled payer-facing behavioral health businesses before.

people.name: Natalia Birgisson, M.D.
people.bio: CEO of Flourish Health; built her career around the communities Flourish serves, with experiences in pediatric emergency rooms that inspired the company's mission to provide more robust services so children don't reach crisis and need hospitalization.

people.name: Natalia Birgisson, MD
people.bio: Stanford-trained physician who worked on the frontlines of pediatric emergency rooms; previously Director of Strategy at Doximity where she helped build and scale tools used by over 80% of U.S. physicians. She founded Flourish Health after losing a young patient to suicide in the pediatric ER, aiming to provide more robust services so kids don't reach crisis and need hospitalization.

people.name: Alexander Xi
people.bio: Alexander Xi (also referred to as Alex Xi) is one of the three co-founders of FlowGPT, alongside Jay Dang and Lifan Wang. The founding idea took shape in late 2022, and the website prototype was completed and launched within three days in January 2023.

people.name: Jay Dang
people.bio: Born Jiacheng Dang, Jay Dang grew up coding, published a paper on AI-assisted glaucoma detection in high school, and enrolled in Computer Science at UC Berkeley before dropping out. He interned at four startups in his first semester and previously attempted an AI-driven A/B testing platform for advertising. He co-founded FlowGPT in January 2023 with Lifan Wang and Alex Xi, building the prototype in three days; the site hit 14,000 users within a week and millions within months. He is described as the youngest AI startup founder in that cohort, raising capital from DCM and Goodwater Capital, and appears on his LinkedIn as 'Founder @ Kaon (prev. FlowGPT)' with the motto 'stay hungry, stay hustle'.

people.name: Lifan Wang
people.bio: Lifan Wang (UC Berkeley Haas MBA '22) is a former engineering manager at Amazon and co-founder of FlowGPT. He met co-founder Jay Dang at UC Berkeley and, in a Berkeley Haas interview, described how the two were power users of ChatGPT who spent around 10 hours a day exploring prompts and interviewed roughly 100 people across online communities before launching FlowGPT as a dedicated platform for prompt creators. He has also served as a recruiting contact for the company (lifan@flowgpt.com).

people.name: Iyinoluwa Aboyeji
people.bio: Nigerian entrepreneur who co-founded Flutterwave in 2016 with Olugbenga Agboola to solve payment infrastructure challenges across Africa.

people.name: Olugbenga "GB" Agboola
people.bio: Nigeria-born entrepreneur and graduate of the MBA program at MIT's Sloan School of Management. Prior to Flutterwave, he worked as an application engineer at PayPal and in product management at Google Wallet. He founded Flutterwave in 2016 to address the fragmented nature of payments in Africa, where cross-border payments remained a hassle.

people.name: Olugbenga Agboola
people.bio: Co-founder of Flutterwave (founded 2016), part of a team of African finance and technology veterans from Standard Bank, PayPal and Google Wallet. Described the Ripple deal as a significant cash investment that will strengthen the company's balance sheet and support its long-term growth plans, and said 'Cross-border value movement is one of the most underserved and highest-growth markets globally right now.'

people.name: Matthew Wright
people.bio: Matthew Wright founded specification data management company Specright over a decade ago and has now developed Forest-PKG alongside a team of packaging and artificial intelligence professionals. He serves as Founder & Executive Chairman and current Forest-PKG CEO, and participated in See Change Sessions on sustainable packaging.

people.name: Jeremy Cai
people.bio: Co-founder of Fountain (founded 2014).

people.name: Keith Ryu
people.bio: Co-founder of Fountain (founded 2014).

people.name: Adrian Kreuziger
people.bio: Co-founder and CTO of Gable; previously led the data department at Convoy, the former Seattle digital trucking startup valued at nearly $4 billion before shutting down in 2023.

people.name: Chad Sanderson
people.bio: Data leader who spent the last decade at the intersection of data infrastructure and enterprise software as a marketer and product strategist, previously working with companies including Convoy and Microsoft, where he led the data department. Co-founded Gable in 2023 to move data accountability upstream with data contracts. Based in the Greater Seattle Area.

people.name: Daniel Dicker
people.bio: Co-founder and founding engineer at Gable; previously part of the data leadership team at Convoy.

people.name: James Frost
people.bio: Co-founder and Chief Product Officer at Gable, part of the founding team building the company's shift left data management platform.

people.name: Daniel Balsam
people.bio: Co-founder and CTO of Goodfire (New York University). Argues that AI safety is now a production engineering problem and that the field needs strong engineers; building toward a future where models are intentionally designed instead of naively scaled.

people.name: Eric Ho
people.bio: Co-founder and CEO of Goodfire (Yale University). Leads the company's mission to use interpretability to understand, learn from, and intentionally design AI systems. Announced the $50M Series A led by Menlo Ventures and the $150M Series B at a $1.25B valuation.

people.name: Tom McGrath
people.bio: Co-founder of Goodfire (Imperial College London), building interpretability tools. Publicly promotes Silico, Goodfire's platform for running long-horizon AI research experiments end to end.

people.name: Chris Tilson
people.bio: Co-founder of Goose with a background in the pet services industry. Previously founded Petbookings.com and operated successful pet services businesses across the U.S. Together with Drew Brinkoetter, brings 31 combined years of pet services industry experience.

people.name: Drew Brinkoetter
people.bio: Co-founder and CEO of Goose. Has a background in the pet services industry, with combined 31 years of pet services experience shared with co-founder Chris Tilson, including operating successful pet services businesses across the U.S.

people.name: Jiahao Xu
people.bio: "We believe investment AI is moving from information assistance to autonomous hypothesis generation and testing," said Jiahao Xu, founder and CEO of GIM. "GIM is building systems that can reason across market data, evaluate signals through feedback, and improve over time in real-world capital markets."

people.name: Ariyan Kabir
people.bio: Co-founded GrayMatter Robotics in 2020 and serves as CEO. States the mission is to 'enhance productivity while prioritizing workforce well-being' through physics-based, AI-powered robotic systems, and describes the company as building 'factory super intelligence' to solve the human bottleneck problem in manufacturing.

people.name: Brual Shah
people.bio: Co-founded GrayMatter Robotics in 2020 alongside Ariyan Kabir and SK Gupta (listed as Brual Shah, Ph.D. in company financing profiles).

people.name: Sangam Pant
people.bio: Co-founder of GrayMatter Robotics; a former corporate executive and co-founder of Evercore Ventures, part of the USC Viterbi-dominated founding team that won the 2020 Maseeh Entrepreneurship Prize Competition.

people.name: Satyandra 'SK' Gupta
people.bio: Co-founded GrayMatter Robotics in 2020 with Ariyan Kabir and Brual Shah (listed as Satyandra Gupta, Ph.D.); the founding team has built a portfolio that includes 10 patents.

people.name: Satyandra K. (SK) Gupta
people.bio: Co-founder and Chief Scientist at GrayMatter Robotics, leading foundational research in physical AI, computational decision-making, and human-centered robotics. Smith International Professor in the Viterbi School of Engineering at USC and founding director of the USC Viterbi Center for Advanced Manufacturing; former Program Director for the National Robotics Initiative at the NSF (2012–2014); author of more than 500 technical articles; Fellow of AAAS, ASME, IEEE, NAI, SME, and the Solid Modeling Association; recipient of the 2026 Thomas Edison Award from ASME.

people.name: Adithya Venkatesh
people.bio: Co-founder of Gushwork, founded the company with Nayrhit Bhattacharya in 2023. Has described Gushwork's solutions as plugging directly into any website to attract both AI agents and human buyers.

people.name: Nayrhit Bhattacharya
people.bio: Co-founder and CEO of Gushwork. Founded the company in 2023 with Adithya Venkatesh, initially helping small and medium businesses outsource workflows using a mix of AI and human expertise, before pivoting to search-led marketing and AI search visibility. Has said the company aims to imagine how marketing and growth will look in an AI-first world and help SMBs generate customers and leads from AI search, describing the shift as 'similar to the early 2000s when everyone was trying to understand SEO for Google.'

people.name: Joe Turner
people.bio: Navy veteran and co-founder/COO of Havoc. Alongside Paul Lwin, founded Havoc two years ago with the conviction that collaborative autonomy would define the future of defense — starting by retrofitting small boats in local waters before scaling into a full company.

people.name: Paul Lwin
people.bio: Co-founder and CEO of Havoc (HavocAI), a company pioneering all-domain collaborative autonomy. A Navy veteran and Myanmar refugee who first saw American uniforms during his evacuation at age 10, he brings a unique perspective to defense innovation, combining military experience with Silicon Valley approaches to national security challenges. Based in Connecticut/Rhode Island; studied at Yale School of Management.

people.name: Anna Rodriguez
people.bio: Worked at Zillow for more than four years, leading teams that managed third-party applications such as Salesforce and Zendesk. Later joined Slalom and was most recently a director at Avalara before launching HeyLibby.

people.name: Spencer Rascoff
people.bio: Former Zillow CEO who co-founded HeyLibby alongside Tony Small and Anna Rodriguez. He is now CEO at Match Group.

people.name: Tony Small
people.bio: Co-founded HeyLibby with former Zillow Group colleague Anna Rodriguez and former Zillow CEO Spencer Rascoff. Previously spent more than several years in senior roles, including at Zillow Group.

people.name: Fred Dom
people.bio: Fred Dom, MSc, is one of the original founders and Chief Executive Officer of HiFiBiO Therapeutics. He is a serial entrepreneur with expertise in private capital investment and biotech formation in the Netherlands, France, and US. Fred holds board positions in Calyxia (France), Kapsera (France) and Oncode Accelerator (Dutch public-private initiative with €325 million funding from National Growth Fund), and is a member of the Advisory Board of Dutch Life Science and Health industry. Previously, he was CEO and co-founder of Saber Bio (created 2021), acquired by a world-leading life science tools company in 2024. Before Saber, he held CEO and CFO positions at HiFiBiO Therapeutics. He holds a B.Sc. and M.Sc. in economics from Erasmus University in Rotterdam.

people.name: Liang Schweizer
people.bio: Dr. Liang Schweizer is Founder, Chairperson and CEO of HiFiBiO Therapeutics, leading the company's mission to unlock the curative powers of the immune system through its DIS® single-cell translational platform. She has spoken on Nasdaq's Live from MarketSite and on the Biotech2050 and Lioness Magazine features about her journey from scientist to first-time CEO and the company's approach to improving the success rate of immunotherapies.

people.name: Liang Schweizer, PhD
people.role: Founder, Chairperson, and CEO (as of January 2024)
people.bio: HiFiBiO Therapeutics Founder, Chairperson, and CEO Liang Schweizer presented the company's proprietary translational DIS® platform in the peer-reviewed journal Drug Discovery Today and sat with Nasdaq to share HiFiBiO's mission to unlock the curative powers of the immune system.

people.name: Geraldine Harriman
people.bio: Co-founder of HotSpot Therapeutics and its Chief Scientific Officer; credited as the founder of the company when it was established in 2017 in Boston.

people.name: Gina Becchetti
people.bio: Listed among the founders of Hypersonix, which was founded in 2018.

people.name: Prem Kiran
people.bio: Serial entrepreneur passionate about building and scaling businesses. An 11-year veteran of SAP before becoming an entrepreneur, he founded Hypersonix in 2018. He is based in the San Francisco Bay Area and associated with Stanford University. He publicly comments on ProfitGPT's five agents (Price, Promo, Inventory, Competitor, Demand) working in orchestration to drive maximized ROI.

people.name: Rama Rao
people.bio: Listed among the founders of Hypersonix, which was founded in 2018.

people.name: Todd Michaud
people.bio: Former IBM executive and former president at Retalix, part of the Hypersonix co-founding team.

people.name: Monish Darda
people.bio: Co-founded Icertis in 2009 with Samir Bodas. Previously co-founded Websym Technologies, helped engineer Storability Software's acquisition by Sun Microsystems, and served as VP of R&D at BladeLogic through its acquisition by BMC Software. He is the company's long-serving CTO and a public voice on responsible AI and the strategic value of contracts.

people.name: Samir Bodas
people.role: Co-founder, former CEO and Executive Chairman
people.bio: Co-founded Icertis in 2009 with Monish Darda. Born in Pune, India, he arrived in the U.S. in 1982 to study at the University of Texas at Austin and began his career as a software programmer at National Instruments. After graduating from Wharton, he joined Microsoft in 1992 in sales and marketing roles, then pursued entrepreneurship at iMandi, Jamcracker, Disha Technology and Aztecsoft. He led Icertis as CEO for more than 15 years, building it into the category leader in contract intelligence, before becoming Executive Chairman in August 2025 to focus on his health. He passed away on January 29, 2026 following a courageous battle with cancer, aged 61.

people.name: Abhinav Shashank
people.bio: Co-founder and CEO of Innovaccer. He frames the company's mission around connecting and curating the world's healthcare information to make it accessible and useful, and argues that with 35-40% of a projected $5-$7.5 trillion in healthcare spending lost to administrative complexity, autonomous operations are an economic necessity. He received IIT Kharagpur's Distinguished Alumnus Award in 2026.

people.name: Kanav Hasija
people.bio: Co-founder of Innovaccer; part of the founding team with Abhinav Shashank and Sandeep Gupta that built the company from a small team into a healthcare cloud platform used by leading health systems.

people.name: Sandeep Gupta
people.bio: Co-founder and President of Innovaccer. He has spoken on rebuilding healthcare for 2030, identifying the absence of a 'context layer'—the middleware connecting fragmented point solutions—as the biggest barrier to autonomous operations at scale.

people.name: Alex Zhavoronkov
people.role: Founder, Chairman, Co-CEO and Chief Business Officer
people.bio: PhD; founded Insilico Medicine in 2014 at the Emerging Technology Centers of Johns Hopkins University in Baltimore, Maryland. He has stated the company was built to treat aging and disease together and to prove that AI can design medicines with real patient impact, and that Insilico is dedicated to extending human productive longevity.

people.name: Alex Zhavoronkov, PhD
people.role: Founder, Chairman, Co-CEO and Chief Business Officer
people.bio: Founded Insilico Medicine in 2014 at the Emerging Technology Centers at Johns Hopkins University in Baltimore. After building a career in the GPU industry in the early 2000s and achieving financial success in semiconductors, he pivoted to biotechnology with the mission of extending healthy, productive human lifespans. He has authored over 310 peer-reviewed papers since 2012, was named to the 2025 Clarivate Highly Cited Researchers list in Pharmacology and Toxicology, serves as adjunct professor of artificial intelligence at the Buck Institute for Research on Aging, co-chairs the Annual Aging Research and Drug Discovery (ARDD) forum, and was named to the inaugural SCW75 list by Scientific Computing World in June 2026. He advocates a vision of 'Pharmaceutical Superintelligence' — a fully autonomous AI platform capable of discovering and designing novel drugs for any disease without human intervention.

people.name: Denitsa Milanova, PhD
people.role: Board of Directors; Founder and CEO of Medici Therapeutics

people.name: Eric Fear
people.bio: Co-founded Inspace XR with Justin Liang in 2017, building augmented and virtual reality tools for the building and architecture sectors.

people.name: Justin Liang
people.bio: Founder and CEO of Inspace (formerly Inspace XR), based in Barangaroo, New South Wales, with 13K LinkedIn followers. A former investor at AMP Ventures specialising in AI, FinTech and AR/VR technologies, he left AMP Ventures to found Inspace in 2017 and made the Forbes 30 under 30 list. He has driven the company's pivot from VR design tools to virtual property inspection and leasing, led its $4m and $6m raises and its push into AI and predictive insights, and has publicly highlighted work with Stockland and equipping CBRE Asia Pacific's office leasing teams with Inspace's virtual leasing platform.

people.name: Adam Pettit
people.bio: Co-founder and CEO of Kandji, now Iru. "Miami is fueling the next frontier for technology advancement. We're thrilled to immerse ourselves in this dynamic community and look forward to welcoming its world-class talent to our expanding team." He has said: "The stack is the problem. With Iru, we collapse the stack and give IT & security teams time and control back."

people.name: Wesley Pettit
people.bio: Co-founder of Iru; listed as founding the company in 2018.

people.name: Dr. Joel Salinas
people.bio: Co-founder and Chief Medical Officer of Isaac Health, described as a world-renowned behavioral neurologist who leads the clinical care team delivering virtual and in-home memory care for patients with Alzheimer's disease and other dementias.

people.name: Julius Bruch
people.bio: Physician-scientist and co-founder/CEO of Isaac Health. Holds a PhD in the molecular biology of neurodegenerative diseases and a medical degree from the University of Cambridge; spent seven years at McKinsey & Company leading projects in value-based care and digital health innovation. Was inspired to work in dementia care partly because his grandmother had an atypical form of dementia.

people.name: Mark Page
people.bio: Aerospace engineer who co-founded JetZero in 2020 with start-up veteran Tom O'Leary, bringing the blended-wing-body (BWB) aerodynamic concept behind the Z4 and the Jet1 Demonstrator.

people.name: Tom O'Leary
people.bio: Start-up veteran who co-founded JetZero in 2020 with aerospace engineer Mark Page. Has led the company's BWB program from concept to a U.S. Air Force-backed full-scale demonstrator, a $175M Series B and a North Carolina manufacturing build-out. Says the Z4 design 'addresses positively all those constraints in a more profound way than the existing tube and wing platform' and that the enterprise is now 'real' and 'viable.'

people.name: A. J. Loiacono
people.bio: Co-Founder and CEO of Judi Health & Judi Rx. After eight years auditing PBM contracts, he concluded the only way to reform the system was to rebuild it from scratch. In 2017 he co-founded Capital Rx (now Judi Rx) on two principles: never profit from drug spend and build technology efficient enough to sustain the business without hidden fees. Today Judi Health manages care and processes claims for over 58 million covered lives with a 99% client retention rate.

people.name: AJ Loiacono
people.bio: Co-Founder and CEO of Judi Health & Capital Rx. Founded the company in 2017 to change how prescription drugs are priced and how pharmacy benefits are administered. Has stated, "Judi Health is not just the promise of better care; it is the technology that powers the future of U.S. healthcare."

people.name: Ryan Kelly
people.bio: Co-founder of Capital Rx (now Judi Health), founded in 2017 alongside CEO AJ Loiacono.

people.name: Chiranjeev (CJ) Kalra
people.bio: Co-founder and Chief Technology Officer of Karman Industries, leading development of its proprietary thermal technology. Formerly Head of Technology at Antora Energy and VP of Power Generation at Heliogen.

people.name: David Tearse
people.bio: Co-founder and CEO of Karman Industries. Formerly at aerospace startup Skyryse and a venture partner/entrepreneur-in-residence at Riot Ventures. Background in aerospace engineering; leads Karman's mission to build next-generation thermal infrastructure applying rocket-engine turbomachinery, EV power electronics and advanced manufacturing to industrial heat and AI data center cooling.

people.name: Ashish Sonone
people.bio: Part of the founding team of Khatabook, the Bengaluru-based fintech bookkeeping startup.

people.name: Dhanesh Kumar
people.bio: Part of the founding team of Khatabook, which helps small shopkeepers and kirana owners manage accounts through a digital ledger.

people.name: Jaideep Poonia
people.bio: Part of the founding team of Khatabook, India's digital ledger app for small businesses.

people.name: Ravish Naresh
people.bio: IIT Bombay graduate and serial entrepreneur; previously co-founded Housing.com (merged with PropTiger in 2017). Founded Khatabook in 2018/2019 and leads it as CEO, driving the mission of creating the biggest and most trusted business platform for Indian MSMEs.

people.name: Vaibhav Kalpe
people.bio: Co-founder of Khatabook, the company later acquired by Kyte Technologies in 2018; after the acquisition, Kalpe joined the Kyte team.

people.name: Irina
people.bio: Named as Knox CEO in the $25M Series A announcement ("said Knox CEO Irina"), quoted on expanding federal authorization capacity while extending the platform to commercial adoption.

people.name: Tess K
people.bio: Co-founder of Knox Systems, founded in 2025, which operates as a provider of a FedRAMP compliance platform for SaaS companies.

people.name: Tess K Frazier
people.bio: Co-founder of Knox Systems, founded in 2025, which operates as a provider of a FedRAMP compliance platform for SaaS companies.

people.name: Cynthia Chaerunnisa
people.bio: Co-founded Kopi Kenangan in 2017 alongside Edward Tirtanata and James Prananto.

people.name: Edward Tirtanata
people.bio: Co-founded Kopi Kenangan in 2017 with James Prananto after realising that major coffee chains in Indonesia were too expensive for the average Indonesian. Grew up in Jakarta, moved to the US in 2007 to study finance and accounting at Northeastern University in Boston; has been an entrepreneur since childhood, selling Pokémon cards and gaming bots at school. As Group CEO he has scaled the Jakarta-based business from a local coffee stall to a venture-backed unicorn with more than 1,300 stores across seven markets, and has increased his personal stake in the company as it expands regionally.

people.name: James Prananto
people.bio: Co-founded Kopi Kenangan in 2017 alongside Edward Tirtanata; serves as Co-CEO and was one of the co-founders officiating the brand's first Singapore outlet (Kenangan Coffee) at Raffles City Shopping Centre.

people.name: Brian Rieger
people.bio: Co-founded Labelbox in 2018 with Manu Sharma and Dan Rasmuson. Extremely technical, with a background in aerospace and software engineering. Met co-founders during senior year capstone aircraft design course at Embry-Riddle. On Labelbox: 'When you look at all of the different sectors of the economy today, there's a lot of visual decision-making going on.'

people.name: Dan Rasmuson
people.bio: Co-founded Labelbox in 2018 alongside Manu Sharma and Brian Rieger. Brings a background in aerospace and software engineering; the founding team spent their earliest days on deep customer discovery rather than building an early prototype.

people.name: Manu Sharma
people.bio: Engineer, designer and entrepreneur. Founded Labelbox in 2018 with long-time friends and colleagues Brian Rieger and Dan Rasmuson. Previously developed computer vision and analytics products at Planet Labs and was one of the earliest engineers at DroneDeploy, where he designed systems for flying drones over the internet and led creation of its app marketplace. Co-founded Ardulab, an open-source platform for experiments aboard the International Space Station, and a renewable energy company. Studied aerospace engineering at Embry-Riddle Aeronautical University and Stanford University, with study across robotics, electrical engineering, computer science and industrial design. A pilot who learned to fly with Dick Rutan. Born in Roorkee, India.

people.name: Nicholas Rioux
people.bio: Labviva's CTO and Co-Founder, and the architect of the company's SLM-first approach. He has been candid that general-purpose LLMs carry extremely high price-per-question economics and maximum hallucination rates on specialty information, and that they aren't trained on the context scientific procurement requires — which is why Labviva builds and trains its own small language models on customer-specific context to improve accuracy and lower the cost of using agents.

people.name: Siamak Baharloo
people.bio: Co-founder and CEO of Labviva. He frames the company's mission around removing a big, time-consuming task that pulls researchers away from doing science in their labs: finding and buying the right supplies for their experiments. He has said Labviva is not focused on displacing existing procurement systems like Jaggaer and Coupa, but on working with them so researchers can access what they need in one place.

people.name: Michael Balaban
people.bio: Co-founder of Lambda. Took on the Chief Product Officer role in May 2026, leading product execution to connect Lambda's infrastructure to the developers and enterprises that rely on it.

people.name: Robert Brooks
people.role: Founding team member and Vice President of Revenue

people.name: Stephen Balaban
people.bio: Co-founder of Lambda, which launched in 2012 out of a San Francisco apartment. Leads Lambda's technology vision, product strategy, and technology development full-time as CTO since May 2026; previously CEO. Based in Palo Alto, California and studied at the University of Michigan.

people.name: Bryce Smith
people.bio: Founder and CEO of LevelTen Energy, based in Seattle, Washington, and an alumnus of the UW Foster School of Business. Smith brings nearly 15 years of experience in the energy industry, having previously spent two years executing a power sale to a corporate customer before founding LevelTen to remove friction between renewable energy buyers and sellers. He has described the company's mission as 'democratizing' the market by creating portfolios of projects that let smaller buyers purchase slices of different projects, and has said LevelTen operates a 'technology-enabled, two-sided marketplace that connects large-scale wind and solar projects with corporate energy buyers.' He was named in GeekWire's 'Working Geek' feature and the WSJ reported on his company's backing from Google and oil-and-gas investors.

people.name: Alex Cyriac
people.bio: Co-founder and CEO of Lively, Inc. Alex started Lively with Shobin Uralil in 2015-2016 after his mother stopped taking essential medication when her insurance copays rose; he has said Lively is growing 4 times faster than legacy HSA incumbents and would become the fastest HSA provider ever to cross $1 billion in assets.

people.name: Shobin Uralil
people.bio: Co-founder and COO of Lively, Inc., based in the New York City Metropolitan Area and an MIT Sloan School of Management alumnus. He and Alex Cyriac served as Lively's first two support representatives for its first 1,000 account holders. He writes about board meetings, the founder-to-executive transition, and Lively milestones such as the Inc. 5000 and the Lively Axis agentic AI rollout.

people.name: Kunal Girotra
people.bio: Energy-industry executive and founder of Lunar Energy; earlier leadership roles at Tesla/SolarCity and Sunrun.

people.name: Martin Zhang
people.bio: Founder of MacroLux Medical. Stated: "We deeply appreciate B Capital's trust and support. In just a few years, MacroLux Medical has developed a robust product portfolio spanning urology, airway management, and gynecology, delivering leading performance and earning widespread recognition from clients and industry leaders alike. This funding will enable us to further extend our global reach and deliver more advanced clinical solutions to clients worldwide."

people.name: Xiaodong Zhang
people.bio: Founder of MediTrust Health (Shanghai MediTrust Technology Co., Ltd.), China's leading healthcare platform that links pharmaceutical companies, insurers, hospitals and patients.

people.name: Sanjeev Barnwal
people.bio: Co-founder and CTO of Meesho, the engineering brain behind Meesho's technology infrastructure, logistics systems and product architecture. An IIT Delhi alumnus with prior corporate experience, he left his job in July 2015 with Vidit Aatrey to found the startup originally launched as Fashnear. He and Vidit have remained with the company since founding, a stability that has helped Meesho weather tough times.

people.name: Vidit Aatrey
people.bio: Co-founder and CEO of Meesho, the more publicly visible of the two founders, handling investor relations, media and strategic direction. An IIT Delhi electrical engineering alumnus, he hails from a middle-class family in Meerut/Uttar Pradesh (father worked at Delhi Jal Board). He previously worked at ITC and then in the strategy team at InMobi before leaving his job in July 2015 to build a startup. Recognitions include Fortune 40 Under 40 (2021), Economic Times 40 Under 40 (2021), Forbes 30 Under 30 (2018, India and Asia list), Entrepreneur 35 Under 35 (2019), India's Most Innovative Company (2020) by Fast Company, and Young Turk Startup of the Year (2020) by CNBC. On a mission to democratise internet commerce for 1 billion Indian consumers, 60 million small businesses and millions of logistics entrepreneurs.

people.name: Jason Tu
people.bio: Co-founder and CEO of MioTech, founded in 2016. Born and raised in China; graduated from Purdue University, received a master's degree from the Toulouse School of Economics and an MBA from Stanford. Previously worked at Standard Chartered Bank and at startups WeLab and RobinHood before returning to Asia. He met co-founder Tao Liu on a ski trip in Lake Tahoe.

people.name: Jason Tu (Jianyu Tu)
people.bio: Co-founder and CEO of MioTech. Commenting on ESG data availability in the region, he said: "People think that there's no data on ESG in this region. That's a misconception. There's a lot of data, it's just not organised."

people.name: Tao Liu
people.bio: Co-founder of Mio Tech, the company founded in 2016 and based in Shanghai/Hong Kong.

people.name: Ketan Patel
people.bio: Co-founder and CEO of Mswipe Technologies Pvt. Ltd. Recognised as one of the Top 25 CEOs in India'24 by the Great Manager Institute. Based in Mumbai; states that 'execution in any business or venture is more important than strategy.'

people.name: Manish Patel
people.bio: Founder of Mswipe Technologies, the mobile POS network provider founded in 2011 that lets merchants accept card payments through smartphones or ordinary feature phones.

people.name: Keegan Harper
people.bio: Co-founder of Nalu Medical, the Carlsbad-based developer of a neurostimulation system for managing intractable chronic pain.

people.name: Lee Hartley
people.bio: Co-founder of Nalu Medical, the Carlsbad-based developer of a neurostimulation system for managing intractable chronic pain.

people.name: Abhijeet Vijayvergiya
people.bio: Co-founder and CEO of Nektar.ai. Previously a sales rep, sales manager and VP of Sales, he founded Nektar.ai in November 2020 to fix falling sales rep productivity and help teams move from founder-led sales to a predictable sales engine. Educated at the Indian Institute of Technology, Kharagpur; his career path described as CS -> AE -> Sales Manager -> VP Sales -> Board Member. Based in Singapore, he speaks publicly on enterprise AI precision and data quality.

people.name: Aravind Ravi Sulekha
people.bio: Co-founder of Nektar.ai, described as an ex-Zendesk tech leader who co-founded the company with Abhijeet Vijayvergiya in 2020.

people.name: Aravind RS
people.bio: Co-founder of Nektar.ai, the connected revenue enablement platform for B2B sales and productivity founded in 2020 and headquartered in Singapore.

people.name: Moran Snir
people.bio: Cofounder and CEO of Nest Genomics. Part of a team of product experts, genetic counselors, seasoned engineers and serial entrepreneurs in the genomics space who previously built Clear Genetics — including the GIA chatbot that served millions of patients — acquired by Invitae in 2019. Featured in the Diagnostic Guru podcast discussing her entrepreneurial spirit, female leadership, and clinical AI.

people.name: Chao Zhang
people.bio: Co-founder and COO at NeuShen Therapeutics; University of Chinese Academy of Sciences. Highlights team milestones including the first patient dosed in the Phase 2 trial of NS-136.

people.name: Joan (Huaqiong) Shen
people.bio: M.D., Ph.D.; ~15 years of drug development (Phase I–IV) experience across large pharma; founded NeuShen and leads the company's mission to develop novel therapies for patients with CNS disorders.

people.name: Lingyun Wu
people.bio: Listed among the co-founders of NeuShen, a developer of drugs for neurological and psychiatric diseases.

people.name: Mike Poole
people.bio: Listed among the co-founders of NeuShen, a developer of drugs for neurological and psychiatric diseases.

people.name: Boxian Tan
people.bio: Singaporean co-founder of Ninja Van Group, established in 2014 alongside Lai Chang Wen and Shaun Chong, originating from the trio's shared frustrations as e-commerce sellers learning that delivery was the hardest part of the business.

people.name: Lai Chang Wen
people.bio: A former derivatives trader at Barclays who quit banking to build a men's made-to-measure fashion line, Marcella, with friends Boxian Tan and Shaun Chong. The pain of fulfilling those orders led the trio to found Ninja Van in 2014. He has led the company from a startup delivering a million parcels a day to roughly two million daily across Southeast Asia, and is driving its diversification into B2B restocking and cold chain.

people.name: Shaun Chong
people.bio: Singaporean co-founder of Ninja Van Group, established in 2014 alongside Lai Chang Wen and Boxian Tan, after the founders experienced supply-chain pain running their own fashion e-commerce business.

people.name: Tan Boxian
people.bio: Co-founder of Ninja Van, established in Singapore in 2014 together with Lai Chang Wen and Shaun Chong.

people.name: Greg Coffey
people.bio: Co-founder of Nuvig Therapeutics; also an angel investor in one startup.

people.name: Greg Coffey, Ph.D.
people.role: Cofounder & Vice President, Immunology & Clinical Translational Research
people.bio: Cofounder of Nuvig Therapeutics and Vice President of Immunology & Clinical Translational Research.

people.name: Pamela Conley
people.role: Co-Founder, Chief Scientific Officer and founding Chief Executive Officer
people.bio: Co-founder of Nuvig Therapeutics and its Chief Scientific Officer and founding CEO. She has described the company's goal as restoring normal immune homeostasis rather than broadly suppressing the immune system, and has led Nuvig since its 2022 launch and $47 million initial financing.

people.name: Pamela Conley, Ph.D.
people.bio: Cofounder and Chief Scientific Officer of Nuvig Therapeutics; served as founding CEO. Has over 30 years' experience in biotech with major achievements in research, therapy development, and corporate leadership. Commented that NVG-2089 is meant to help "restore normal immune homeostasis" instead of "leaving people's immune systems crippled and not able to respond to foreign antigens."

people.name: Sheldon Koenig
people.bio: Listed as a cofounder of Nuvig Therapeutics, a company founded in 2022.

people.name: Dane Atkinson
people.bio: Listed among Odeko's employees on the company's LinkedIn page.

people.name: Tim Griffin
people.bio: Founder of Cloosiv, the mobile ordering app for coffee shops launched in 2017, which merged with Odeko in 2020 under the Odeko name.

people.name: Evan Fein
people.bio: Listed among Omnidian's employees/founders; part of the team that launched the company in 2016.

people.name: Jon Guerster
people.bio: Listed among Omnidian's employees/founders; part of the team that launched the company in 2016.

people.name: Mark Liffmann
people.bio: CEO and co-founder of Omnidian. One of three solar industry veterans who started Omnidian in 2016 with the mission to protect and accelerate investments in clean energy.

people.name: Mike Dooley
people.bio: Listed among Omnidian's employees/founders; part of the team that launched the company in 2016.

people.name: Lalitha Rajagopalan
people.bio: Co-founder leading operations and strategy (also described as Head of Strategy and GTM). Explains that ORO began with the question of what was not working in procurement technology, finding legacy systems were built for transactions rather than the full engagement journey across employees, suppliers and internal stakeholders.

people.name: Sudhir Bhojwani
people.bio: Co-founder and CEO of ORO Labs, a former SAP Ariba product leader. Says demand for orchestration has skyrocketed because procurement teams are under tremendous pressure to move faster, to save more, and to make employee and supplier experiences easier. Believes procurement is massively inefficient today and that legacy systems were built to do an approval flow, not to support the full engagement journey.

people.name: Yuan Tung
people.bio: Co-founder and CTO of ORO Labs, focused on redesigning how people, systems and suppliers work together through agentic workflows, orchestration and AI in enterprise procurement technology.

people.name: Anniek Schouten
people.bio: Co-founded Overstory with Indra den Bakker in Lisbon in 2018 to help solve the climate crisis; listed as COO and Co-founder.

people.name: Indra den Bakker
people.bio: Co-founder of Overstory (formerly 20tree.ai); previously listed as CEO and Co-Founder. Greentown Boston notes he passed away.

people.name: Indrajeet Virkar
people.bio: Co-founder and chief executive of Overstory, leading the company's work applying satellite imagery and machine learning to vegetation intelligence for utilities and telecoms.

people.name: Roelof Pieters
people.bio: Co-founder and Chief Technology Officer of Overstory.

people.name: Jonathan Zhu
people.bio: Co-founded PaleBlueDot AI in 2024. Listed by GetLatka as founder/CEO, and by Caproasia as co-founder.

people.name: Shaodong Huang
people.bio: Co-founded PaleBlueDot AI in 2024, per Hoodline.

people.name: Sheldon Huang
people.bio: Listed as a co-founder of PaleBlueDot AI (Palo Alto, California). Posted about the team achieving NVIDIA Exemplar Cloud status for production-ready AI infrastructure on NVIDIA B300 systems, and shared team hiring activity.

people.name: Hendra Kwik
people.bio: Co-founder and chief executive of Payfazz, guiding the company's agent-based financial services network for Indonesia's underbanked segments.

people.name: Jefriyanto
people.bio: Co-founded Payfazz in 2016, a fintech platform aiming to achieve financial inclusion for unbanked residents in rural Indonesia.

people.name: Ricky Winata
people.bio: Co-founder of Payfazz, involved in product and business strategy for the company's fintech platform and agent network.

people.name: Tianwei Liu
people.role: Deputy CEO, Fazz Financial Group (Co-Founder & CEO of Xfers)

people.name: Eric Boduch
people.bio: Co-founder of Pendo, where he spent eight years helping grow the software company into a fixture on the Raleigh skyline. He departed in early 2022 to launch 24 and Up, a Raleigh-based startup venture studio aiming to co-create 15 companies over five to seven years, focused on making the first 24 months of a startup as productive as possible.

people.name: Erik Troan
people.bio: Co-founder and CTO of Pendo, one of the four co-founders who built the company from a team of 12 into a Raleigh unicorn.

people.name: Rahul Jain
people.role: VP of Business Development and Co-Founder
people.bio: Co-founder and VP of Business Development at Pendo, part of the four-person founding team alongside Todd Olson, Erik Troan, and Eric Boduch.

people.name: Todd Olson
people.bio: CEO and co-founder of Pendo. Before Pendo, he was VP of Product at Rally Software, which he joined via the acquisition of a startup he founded, where he effectively served as CTO and head of product. He has said The Four Steps to the Epiphany by Steve Blank shaped much of his thinking around product-market fit and customer discovery.

people.name: Nelson Chu
people.bio: Founded Percent in 2018 and serves as its founder and CEO. He has described Percent as a company designed to facilitate private-credit transactions for capital-markets type deals from end to end, covering sourcing, structuring, syndication, surveillance, and servicing.

people.name: Amit Bareket
people.bio: Co-founded Perimeter 81 in 2018 and serves as its Chief Executive Officer, leading the company's cloud-native SASE and zero-trust network security strategy.

people.name: Sagi Gidali
people.bio: Co-founded Perimeter 81 in 2018 and leads product, driving the development of the company's converged SASE platform.

people.name: Andy Konwinski
people.bio: Co-founder of Perplexity AI and co-creator of Apache Spark and Databricks co-founder; involved in the company's early technical and strategic direction.

people.name: Aravind Srinivas
people.bio: Co-founder and CEO of Perplexity AI. Previously a research scientist at OpenAI and DeepMind, and a PhD in computer science from UC Berkeley focused on deep reinforcement learning and generative models.

people.name: Denis Yarats
people.bio: Co-founder and CTO of Perplexity AI. Former AI research scientist at Meta AI (FAIR) and previously at Quora; PhD in computer science from NYU working on deep reinforcement learning.

people.name: Johnny Ho
people.bio: Co-founder and Chief Strategy Officer of Perplexity AI. Previously a quantitative researcher/trader at Tower Research Capital and an early engineer at Quora.

people.name: Benji Bernstein
people.bio: Co-founder of Phenom.

people.name: Brad Goldoor
people.bio: Co-founder and Chief People Officer of Phenom. Publicly discussed the company's $22M Series B and plans to hire roughly 150 people to fuel global expansion of sales, marketing and product.

people.name: Hari Bayireddi
people.bio: Co-founder of Phenom, involved in the company's product and technology direction.

people.name: Hari Bayireddy
people.bio: Co-founded Phenom in 2010 alongside Mahe Bayireddi and Brad Goldoor; serves as Chief Operating Officer.

people.name: Mahe Bayireddi
people.bio: Co-founder and Chief Executive Officer of Phenom, leading the company's AI-powered talent experience platform strategy.

people.name: Noga Leviner
people.bio: Co-founded PicnicHealth in 2014 and served as CEO for more than a decade before transitioning to an active role on the board of directors. In her mid-twenties she began a long road to a Crohn's disease diagnosis, an experience that inspired PicnicHealth. She is based in San Francisco and studied at Stanford University.

people.name: Troy Astorino
people.bio: Co-founder and CTO of PicnicAI, focused on building AI that simplifies and accelerates clinical research and care delivery. Based in San Francisco; studied at MIT.

people.name: Eiso Kant
people.bio: Founder and former CTO of source{d}, a company applying machine learning to source code analysis; co-founded Poolside in 2023 and leads its technical/model research organization.

people.name: Jason Warner
people.bio: Former CTO of GitHub (2017-2021) and prior engineering leadership roles at Heroku and Canonical; co-founded Poolside in 2023 to build frontier AI models purpose-built for software engineering.

people.name: Mike Suiters
people.bio: Co-founder and CEO of Positive Development and a former Deloitte executive. Leads the company's mission to expand accessible, relationship-based developmental autism care and has driven over $100M in total fundraising.

people.name: Benjamin Rapoport
people.bio: Neurosurgeon-engineer and former Neuralink co-founder who holds a PhD in electrical engineering from MIT and has been developing brain-computer interfaces for more than 15 years. A neurosurgeon at Mount Sinai, he works to bridge the gap between engineers and the people who stand to benefit from BCI technology.

people.name: Mark Hettick
people.bio: Co-founder and VP of Engineering at Precision Neuroscience. His team pushes the boundaries of science to develop materials that safely live in the body long-term.

people.name: Michael Mager
people.bio: Co-founder and CEO of Precision Neuroscience. Has a background spanning technology, finance and healthcare; holds an AB in Latin from Harvard University and an MPhil in Economic History from the University of Cambridge, and is a chartered financial analyst charterholder. Before co-founding Precision, he built and invested in technology-enabled businesses across several industries, and is co-founder and co-chairman of Assembly Software.

people.name: Arik Shtilman
people.bio: Co-founder and Chief Executive Officer of Rapyd. He leads the company's global fintech-as-a-service strategy and its expansion of cross-border payments, payouts and embedded finance infrastructure. A long-time payments and technology entrepreneur, he has been the public face of Rapyd's fundraising and product announcements.

people.name: Arkady Karpman
people.bio: Co-founder of Rapyd, involved in building the company's core technology and engineering organization behind its payments, wallet and issuing APIs.

people.name: Omer Priel
people.bio: Co-founder of Rapyd; previously listed as Vice President of Business Development and currently VP Rapyd DNA.

people.name: Ioannis Alexandros Antonoglou
people.bio: Former Google DeepMind researcher (DeepMind/Gemini background); co-founded Reflection AI in 2024 to build frontier open-source AI.

people.name: Ioannis Antonoglou
people.bio: Employee #25 at Google DeepMind, in the room for AlphaGo's iconic 'Move 37', and instrumental in AlphaGo, AlphaZero and MuZero. Co-founded Reflection AI in 2024 with Misha Laskin. Carries the early DeepMind 'AGI as a serious research program' ethos and leads the technical buildout, including large-scale Mixture-of-Experts training and the Beam open-weight model.

people.name: Misha Laskin
people.bio: Former Google DeepMind researcher who co-founded Reflection AI in 2024 with Ioannis Antonoglou. Led the company from stealth emergence in March 2025 ($130M, ~$545M valuation) through a $2B raise at an $8B valuation (October 2025) and a $25B pre-money valuation round (April 2026, confirmed by Laskin on CNBC on April 23, 2026). Frames the mission around building open frontier models the West can own.

people.name: Job van der Voort
people.bio: Co-founder and Chief Executive Officer of Remote; previously VP of Product at GitLab and a neuroscientist. Has been the public face of the company's global employment and payroll offering.

people.name: Marcelo Lebre
people.bio: Co-founder of Remote, leading the company's product and engineering organization; earlier served as CTO at GitLab-acquired and other engineering-led software companies.

people.name: Stella (Yibin) Shi
people.role: Founder, Chief Executive Officer and Chair of the Board
people.bio: Founder, CEO and chair of the board of Rona Therapeutics since company inception in 2021, bringing ~15 years of biopharmaceutical industry and venture capital experience. Prior to founding Rona, she was a managing director at Lilly Asia Ventures (LAV) from 2015, with a track record of venture creation.

people.name: Antonio Mallia
people.bio: Founder and CEO of Seltz, a retrieval systems expert who previously worked at Pinecone, Amazon (Alexa search / AGI), and Bloomberg. His PhD work in computer science at New York University focused on information retrieval, and his first published research paper made the query processing algorithms behind large-scale search engines twice as fast.

people.name: David Li
people.bio: Co-founder and CEO of Sharpa. Also co-founder and CEO of Hesai Technology, the world's largest supplier of automotive LiDAR. Founded Sharpa in late 2024 to develop general-purpose robotic platforms. Has stated a long-term goal of lowering robot costs to under USD 5,000 for households.

people.name: Sun Kai
people.bio: Co-founder and Chief Scientist of Sharpa, and co-founder and Chief Scientist of Hesai Technology.

people.name: Xiang Shaoqing
people.bio: Co-founder and CTO of Sharpa, and co-founder and CTO of Hesai Technology.

people.name: Adem Esen
people.bio: Technologist and co-founder/CTO of Shipday, based in New York, New York, United States. Studied at Bilkent University.

people.name: Moin Islam
people.bio: Co-founder and CEO of Shipday. Identified delivery logistics as a critical problem for online businesses and built Shipday's platform; has noted that early adopters helped shape the product and that large brands such as YUM! Brands (KFC) sought its digital delivery solutions.

people.name: Justin Nicols
people.bio: Experienced founder with a demonstrated history of working in information technology; studied at University of Wisconsin-Milwaukee - School of Business Administration. Founded Sift in 2017 to fill a gap in the healthcare payments space after developing a mobile payment app for healthcare and observing the time and dollars wasted on processing and collecting medical bills due to disparate data systems and human-capital-intensive workflows. Brought a data-driven e-commerce background, applying predictive analytics to healthcare payments. Says the biggest hesitancy in founding Sift was building a world-class data science team, which he found in Milwaukee.

people.name: Dr. Jim Ryan
people.bio: Co-founder of SilverCloud Health, contributing the clinical and academic research base behind the company's online mental health programmes.

people.name: Dr. Karen Tierney
people.bio: Co-founder of SilverCloud Health, involved in the clinical programme design and research underpinning the platform.

people.name: Ken Cahill
people.bio: Co-founder and long-serving CEO of SilverCloud Health; led the company from its Trinity College Dublin spin-out to its 2021 acquisition by Amwell, with earlier executive experience in the technology and healthcare sectors.

people.name: Neeraj Jain
people.bio: Co-founder of SolarSquare (founded 2015). Former Investment Analyst at Deutsche Bank AG.

people.name: Nikhil Nahar
people.bio: Co-founder of SolarSquare (founded 2015). Former Senior Manager at Panasonic India.

people.name: Shreya Mishra
people.bio: Co-founder and Chief Executive Officer of SolarSquare; former Co-Founder & CEO of Flyrobe. Described the company's ambition as building 'the operating system for India's energy transition' spanning solar installation, after-sales service, financing, battery solutions and home energy management.

people.name: Dave Johnson
people.bio: Co-founder and CEO of Solve Therapeutics. Previously helped create and led ADC biotech VelosBio, which was acquired by Merck.

people.name: Alex Yin
people.bio: Earned a doctorate in computer music at the University of York. Worked with CEO Shawn Song on multimodal AI at TikTok before co-founding Sonilo.

people.name: Shawn Song
people.bio: Trained at Carnegie Mellon University (CMU) and led multimodal AI technology work at TikTok, where he worked alongside Sonilo CTO Alex Yin. Leads Sonilo's mission to build models that understand the visual story and generate music and sound effects that fit a scene frame by frame.

people.name: Al Ray Tabiliran
people.bio: Co-founder of Spectrumedics, manufacturer of a therapeutic device for the treatment of arterial vascular calcification.

people.name: Elynn Phang
people.bio: Co-founder of Spectrumedics, the Singapore-based developer of the Sonico intravascular shock wave balloon catheter system for arterial vascular calcification.

people.name: Peng Huiqun
people.bio: Co-founder of Spectrumedics, a Singapore medical device company focused on intravascular lithotripsy for calcified arterial lesions.

people.name: Andrew Rush

people.bio: Original Presto co-creator at Facebook and Starburst co-founder, focused on the query engine's core architecture and performance.

people.name: David Phillips
people.bio: Presto co-creator and Starburst co-founder, an engineer on the distributed SQL engine's design and execution.

people.name: Justin Borgman
people.bio: Co-founder and long-time CEO of Starburst; previously co-founder and CEO of Hadapt, which was acquired by Teradata, where he later led the effort that became Starburst.

people.name: Kamil Bajda-Pawlikowski
people.bio: Starburst co-founder and engineering leader, previously at Hadapt/Teradata, working on distributed query processing.

people.name: Martin Traverso
people.bio: One of the original creators of Presto at Facebook and co-founder/CTO of Starburst; a leading maintainer of the Presto and Trino open-source projects.

people.name: Matt Fuller

people.name: Madan Somasundaram
people.bio: Co-founder and CEO of Sugar.fit. Studied at Harvard Business School and brings experience across global finance and entrepreneurship, with a strong foundation in strategy, operations and long-term value creation. At Sugar.fit he focuses on integrating medical science, data intelligence and human coaching to enable sustainable metabolic health outcomes, and on building evidence-based, consumer-first health solutions.

people.bio: Co-founder of sugar.fit, a diabetes care and reversal program provider founded in 2021.

people.name: Somasundaram Madan
people.bio: Co-founder of sugar.fit, a diabetes care and reversal program provider founded in 2021.

people.name: Brian Wallach
people.bio: Co-Founder of Synapticure. Diagnosed with ALS in August 2017 at age 36/37; former federal prosecutor in Chicago. With his wife Sandra Abrevaya he co-founded I AM ALS and Synapticure to build the proactive, patient-centered care they could not find. Their story is documented in the film No Ordinary Campaign.

people.name: Sandra Abrevaya
people.bio: Co-Founder and CEO of Synapticure, a leader in neurodegenerative virtual care. Also Co-Founder and board member of I AM ALS, the patient-led advocacy organization she established with her husband, Brian Wallach, after his ALS diagnosis in 2017. Caregiver to Brian and mother to their two daughters. Previously president and chief impact officer of Thrive Chicago, a founding CEO in the nonprofit sector, and held senior roles with the City of Chicago, the White House, U.S. Department of Education, U.S. Senate, and U.S. House of Representatives. Executive producer and subject of the documentary 'For Love and Life: No Ordinary Campaign.'

people.name: Andreas Bibl
people.bio: Co-founder and CEO of Tacta Systems, leading the company's development of "Dexterous Intelligence" technology that gives robots human-level tactile skills and spatial awareness.

people.name: Cheryl Sew Hoy
people.bio: Founder and CEO of Tiny Health, building a precision microbiome platform that helps people of all ages understand and optimize their gut and vaginal microbiomes, from early life through adulthood and into healthy longevity. Before Tiny Health, she was an EIR at SVB, founded multiple startups, advised healthtech, blockchain and education companies, and co-founded #MovingForward. In January 2026 she was appointed to the Texas Nutrition Advisory Committee (4-year term through September 1, 2029). Her work has been featured by TIME, CNN, Washington Post, Bloomberg, Fox News and CNBC.

people.name: Esteban Castaño
people.bio: Co-founder and CEO of TRM Labs. Previously worked in product and strategy roles in technology and financial services, and co-founded the company in 2018 with Rahul Raina to bring compliance-grade intelligence to crypto.

people.name: Rahul Raina
people.bio: Co-founder and CTO of TRM Labs, leading the engineering and data-science teams that build the company's blockchain intelligence, risk-scoring, and cross-chain analytics platform.

people.name: Kaare Wagner
people.bio: Turbine co-founder and advisory board member; associated with SVB.

people.name: Mike Hurst
people.bio: Fintech veteran and former CEO/founder of Exactuals (payments startup sold to City National Bank in 2018). After the 2022 tech market reset left him short of free cash for capital calls, he conceived Turbine as a credit product letting LPs borrow against their VC fund stakes; also a venture partner with TTV Capital.

people.bio: Listed by Tracxn as the founder and CEO of Unblocked Brands, which he founded in 2021.

Vivacta is committed to advancing innovative in vivo CAR-T cell therapies. Our core product, GT801, has demonstrated promising safety and efficacy profiles in early clinical studies across hematological malignancies and autoimmune disease patients, potentially offering these patient populations a transformative treatment option to deliver innovative therapies to more patients in need." Also quoted on GT801 data: "We are encouraged by the promising safety profile and compelling efficacy signals observed with GT801 in heavily pretreated NHL patients."

people.role: Founder and Chair of Scientific Advisory Committee

Famous for discovering the PI3K pathway and its role in cancer, and previously founded Agios and Petra Pharma. He mentored Samuel Bakhoum and co-founded Volastra based on the chromosomal instability findings.

people.name: Olivier Elemento, Ph.D.
people.bio: Founder and Scientific Advisor at Volastra Therapeutics; Director of the Englander Institute for Precision Medicine at Weill Cornell Medicine. He is one of the three partners who turned the chromosomal instability research into Volastra Therapeutics.

people.name: Samuel Bakhoum, M.D., Ph.D.
people.bio: Co-founder and Chief Scientific Officer of Volastra Therapeutics. While at Memorial Sloan Kettering, he noticed that lagging chromosomes appeared more often in metastatic cancers than in primary cancers, and pursued the research in Lewis Cantley's lab at Cornell, which became the scientific basis for Volastra's founding.

people.name: Jordan Glazier
people.bio: Jordan Glazier founded Wildfire Systems in 2017 and serves as its CEO. He began his career as a consultant with the Boston Consulting Group, after which he joined GATX Corporation where he ran international business development and built a new multinational business unit providing multi-modal transportation and logistics services. He then became an early executive at eBay, where he built several of eBay's largest business units from the ground up, including marketplaces for consumer electronics, computers and industrial equipment. After eBay, he was COO of Client Shop (acquired by Internet Brands) and then joined Eventful, Inc., which he built into the world's largest discovery platform for local events and entertainment (acquired by CBS). He holds a degree from Northwestern University - Kellogg School of Management.
